attempted_claim: Let (X_a, C_a) and (X_b, C_b) be the Brown-Wemyss GV-fail pair of projective flopping contractions of quasi-projective Gorenstein terminal Calabi-Yau threefolds, each with a single irreducible rational flopping curve, identical genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants, non-isomorphic classical contraction algebras A_a, A_b, and flops (X_a^+, X_b^+) with Bridgeland-Chen flop-flop autoequivalences Phi_a = F_a^+ \circ F_a on Perf(X_a), Phi_b = F_b^+ \circ F_b on Perf(X_b) given by fibre-product Fourier-Mukai kernels. Let D_a, D_b in Perf of the respective squares be the Booth derived-contraction-algebra twist kernels enhancing the classical J-twist kernels. Settle by proof or rigorous disproof: are the derived twist data distinguished, i.e. is dim HH^2(D_a) \neq dim HH^2(D_b) (equivalently, do Phi_a and Phi_b induce non-matching Hochschild-cohomology traces), so that the derived Fourier-Mukai twist refines the identical GV pair? A complete answer proves the Hochschild inequality with explicit computed dimensions or proves equality with a rigorous quasi-isomorphism argument on the derived level.
claim_type: Hochschild inequality vs equality of derived twist kernels, proof or disproof
decisive_failure: The investigation was limited to literature grounding in Brown-Wemyss and Booth sources plus bounded in-lane linear algebra; no computer-algebra engine (Singular, Macaulay2, QPA) was available, no global projective Calabi-Yau completions of the local flop pair were supplied, and no derived A-infinity or Hochschild-resolution computation for the new flop exists in the citable literature, so no HH^2 inequality or equality proof could be audited.
domain: algebraic geometry, derived categories of threefolds
